notes:
The benchmark calls the real FilterSet the way the voice does: setConfig per block, then renderLong (mono) or renderLongStereo (128 frames). It starts with 10 blocks of warm-up and then measures 10 blocks. quickLog and instantTan are pulled out of functions.cpp with sed during the build. Only one stub was needed, stubs/processing/engines/audio_engine.h with cpuDireness.

Compiles on the PC (g++) and on ARM. On the PC the UBSan check for signed overflow is switched off, because the filters overflow on purpose. Every case prints an output hash, which lets you check whether a change stays bit-exact. Compare the hashes only ARM against ARM: on the PC the fallback version of smmulr does not round, so the values differ.

Morph and drive:
- Ladder morph costs nothing extra. From about 10% resonance the ladder always takes the tanh path (+14 instructions per sample).
- Drive costs 31% more than 24 dB. At high cutoff and resonance, oversampling doubles the cost (2.3%).
- HP morph costs +53 per block. HP resonance above about 50% takes the 2D tanh, which is +48%.

Not recommended: computing L and R in NEON lanes. vqrdmulh rounds differently, so the result would not be bit-exact, and the tanh table needs gathers.

Possible saving in total: LP24 about 15-20%, HP about 20%, SVF about 12%. With 30 voices with a filter that would be around 4-5% CPU.
